domain: Machine Learning / Information Ecology / Computational Epistemology
topic_summary: Analysis of the Elias Thorne phenomenon: a fictional character appearing in 26.5% of AI-generated stories across multiple LLMs, traced to alignment training constraints and dataset recycling. The case exemplifies 'model collapse' or 'AI inbreeding'—degradation of AI outputs when models train on synthetic data from prior models, creating a feedback loop that amplifies quirks and reduces diversity.

key_entities: Elias Thorne (fictional character; appears in 26.5% of sampled AI stories)
Cornell University researchers Sil Hamilton and David Mimno (primary investigators)
WildChat dataset (1M GPT-3.5 conversations; 166 featuring Elias; recycled into training sets)
Major AI labs: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google (models exhibiting phenomenon)
Daniel May (software engineer; first public documentation)
Amazon Kindle store (platform where Elias Thorne appears as author byline)
Alignment training systems (safety guardrails steering away from copyrighted/adult content)
Contemporary published fiction corpus (2,700 novels; baseline for frequency comparison)
key_tensions: Safety alignment vs output diversity (guardrails create safe-but-repetitive generation space)
Synthetic training data availability vs human-generated data scarcity (web increasingly AI-generated)
Model performance optimization vs long-tail distribution preservation (tails disappear under recursive training)
key_claims: Elias appears 900x more frequently in AI stories than in contemporary published fiction
88.3% of generated stories share 11 core tokens (names, professions, locations)
Alignment training to avoid copyrighted characters created inadvertent prominence for 'safe' alternatives
WildChat dataset recycling propagated Elias fixation across industry training pipelines
Model collapse is irreversible once synthetic data dominates training corpus
Character has escaped AI systems into commercial products (Kindle books, YouTube videos)
key_mechanisms: Alignment training filters: steer generation away from copyrighted/adult content toward narrow 'safe' space
Dataset recycling pipeline: WildChat → industry training sets → cross-model propagation
Synthetic data feedback loop: AI outputs → web content → future training data → degraded models
Commercial amplification: AI-generated content published to platforms → further contaminates training corpus
key_absences: No documentation of original Elias Thorne source (pre-WildChat origin unknown)
No industry-wide synthetic data tracking or labeling standard
No mechanism to reverse model collapse once initiated

omegas.description: What is the pre-WildChat origin of Elias Thorne? If traceable to a single human-written story or prompt template, the phenomenon is dataset contamination rather than emergent alignment artifact. If untraceable, suggests spontaneous generation from alignment constraints.

At what synthetic-to-human data ratio does model collapse become irreversible? Cornell paper claims irreversibility but does not quantify threshold. If reversible via high-quality data injection, snare classification weakens to rope.

Is the alignment-diversity tradeoff structurally necessary, or artifact of current RLHF methods? Alternative alignment approaches (constitutional AI, debate, etc.) may preserve diversity while achieving safety. If avoidable, tangled_rope reclassifies to rope.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + F34 check on alignment engineering

omegas.description: Does model collapse affect image/video generation models similarly? Text-only analysis may miss broader pattern. If multimodal collapse follows different dynamics, current framing is domain-specific rather than general AI phenomenon.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) + F14 check

omegas.description: Is Elias Thorne a unique case or representative of broader class of alignment-induced quirks? If unique, phenomenon is anecdotal; if representative, suggests systematic measurement gap in alignment evaluation.
omegas.source: F15 (Premature Closure) on generalization from single case

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: model_collapse_feedback classified as snare with irreversibility claim, but Cornell paper does not quantify reversibility threshold or test recovery via high-quality data injection. Generated omega_reversibility_threshold to bound this uncertainty. No F34: domain (ML training dynamics, information theory) is within model competence. No F14: three lenses applied (ML engineering, information ecology, epistemology). No F15: five candidate axes enumerated; three selected after independence testing.
